# PB-04 staged proposal — review before storage/API changes

Status: proposed next-stage architecture; only the API/schema-preserving projection
increment is approved for implementation. PB-04 remains in progress. This is not
a new qualified storage profile or a promise that an in-process cache solves it.

## Measured problem

PB-03's five-artifact 512-history event case has mean CAS index time 18.104 ms,
including only 0.919 ms of SQL: about 17.185 ms is projection derivation/diff CPU.
Mean CAS snapshot decode is 7.997 ms, load decode 6.493 ms, encode 3.957 ms and
snapshot UPDATE 38.699 ms. Runner wall time outside store load/commit reaches
roughly 15.995 ms p95, including complete canonical serialization for quota.
These are different distributions/stages, not additive percentile claims.

Let S be logical serialized-state bytes, H retained records, W touched records,
A installed catalog bytes and D changed projection bytes. Current full load is
O(S+A); an owned State clone is O(S); quota serialization is O(S); PostgreSQL CAS
decodes the old snapshot again and writes O(S). Index/public projection derivation
materializes two full JSON row sets and keyed maps, O(H) nodes plus payload copies.
The current Storage load/full-CAS interface and arbitrary mutable State closures
cannot honestly guarantee O(W) work while keeping their present implementation.

## Approved first increment: typed borrowed projection deltas

Replace temporary full JSON native/public rows with typed borrowed row identities
and fields. Normalize duplicate identities with the same last-writer semantics
as the existing reference generator. Compare typed fields before deriving JSON;
changed-source candidates reuse canonical public sanitizers, and only actual
changed/deleted rows enter the existing SQL batches. Existing public
sanitizers remain the sole source of public JSON, with a conservative fallback
comparison when a cheap source equality test cannot establish equality.

No database migration, quota rule, encryption context, transition semantics or
Storage signature changes. Keep the old JSON derivation under tests as a reference
oracle, including arbitrary supplied State/index values, removals, receipt-offset
shifts, duplicate row identities, redacted private-field changes and cold index
materialization. Existing database projection parity/security tests must pass.

This first increment still scans O(H) and uses O(H) small borrowed map nodes plus
O(D) retained SQL JSON plus a largest-candidate temporary; it does not claim O(W) time or fix State load/clone/quota serialization.
It should remove most unchanged-row string/JSON allocation and repeated public
projection work. Measure that claim and retained memory rather than marking the
whole task complete from an index-only improvement.

## Next-stage decision: optional versioned working-set/patch storage

A history-independent path requires a different internal transaction boundary.
Keep public full `load` and `compare_and_swap` as compatibility/reference paths;
add a separately versioned capability only after a reviewed design. Existing
callers must not silently receive a partial State or lose arbitrary full-CAS
validation. The default implementation continues the current reference semantics.

A transaction must acquire the same authoritative namespace owner/incarnation and
revision fence, then read a certified complete working set and apply a validated
patch atomically. Changes to events, receipts, waits, children, effects, indexes,
quota counters and the namespace revision commit together. Host dispatch remains
outside storage transactions. There is one logical state owner, not a shadow
editable event engine.

Do not implement a separate fast event-transition algorithm. Extract canonical
pure transition/validation planning used by both reference State and bounded
storage adapters. An initial fast capability can cover no-consumer/no-waiter
admission only if that same canonical planner establishes its applicability;
unsupported operations return an explicit fallback. Differential tests compare
full state, dispositions, IDs, receipts, index choices and refusals after every
step, including duplicate/changed events, epochs, expiry, protection and crashes.
Other transitions remain slow until ported, and PB-04 cannot claim completion
while the required workload matrix still depends on unbounded fallback.

### Authoritative representation and corruption

Normalized per-record PostgreSQL rows are a possible representation, but a SQL
projection's absence is not evidence that no authoritative waiter/event exists.
A design must define authenticated authoritative search/absence, not merely reuse
`runtime_index` as a second source of truth. Derived index drift must either be
verified against the source working set and repaired or fail closed.

One candidate worth prototyping is an immutable, content-addressed canonical data
tree rooted by a versioned namespace header. Point/range reads verify visited
nodes and absence proofs from the authoritative root. A patch replaces only
changed paths; materialized native/public SQL tables stay disposable projections.
This keeps one logical State and permits a full-load compatibility reader. It
also makes exact subtree byte lengths possible, unlike an approximate row-size
ledger. This is an architecture option, not permission to implement it now.

No cache is needed for the first prototype. If a later derived cache is proposed,
its key includes exact root/revision/incarnation/owner context and verified node
identity, with explicit invalidation on ownership loss, rollback and migration.
A metadata-only revision check must not hide changed backing bytes. Selected
records/nodes are freshly integrity/authentication checked; a cold full reader
must detect corrupt retained data. The policy for corruption of untouched history
must be explicit: no O(W) design can also rescan O(S) unrelated bytes on every
operation. Immutable database write guards plus authenticated roots may narrow
that gap, but must be tested rather than presumed.

### Exact quota semantics

Approximate row bytes are insufficient. Preserve the current quota's exact
canonical State byte count or propose an explicit versioned policy that does not
widen the accepted workload. For a canonical JSON tree, contributions are exact:

- scalar: canonical UTF-8 encoding length;
- object: two brace bytes + key JSON bytes + one colon per entry + child lengths
  + max(entry_count - 1, 0) comma bytes;
- array: two bracket bytes + child lengths + max(element_count - 1, 0) commas.

Stored subtree lengths/counts must be integrity bound to the authoritative node
and checked when new nodes are created; updates recompute affected ancestors in
the same transaction. Namespace counters cover runs, events, receipts and queued
destinations exactly. A failed quota check commits neither patch nor counters.
Full-load differential tests must equal the existing canonical serializer byte
for byte after every mutation, including escaped Unicode, empty containers,
array deletion and nested index changes.

Receipt offsets are a specific obstacle: the public State uses a Vec plus numeric
index offsets, so removing earlier receipts can change later offset values and
canonical digit lengths. That cannot be hidden by charging only the deleted row.
Either preserve all affected changes (W may be H for that operation), use an
explicit separately versioned representation with a proved legacy-size adapter,
or keep that maintenance operation on the reference path. The transition's real
complexity bound must say so; no approximate subtraction or quota reset.

### Protection, migration and old callers

A new representation needs migration version 0003 or another explicit profile;
it cannot reuse the old snapshot envelope with different meaning. Protected rows
must authenticate namespace, logical key/type and record/root version. Untouched
records may retain older keys only with explicit key-retention and full-read
requirements. Rotation remains a caller-requested atomic administrative operation
or an explicitly versioned resumable API; ordinary CAS must not silently weaken
`reencrypt_namespace` semantics.

Migration reads/verifies the old snapshot and artifacts under exclusive namespace
ownership, constructs and validates the new representation and exact quota root,
then atomically changes the representation selector. Interrupted migration must
leave the old selector valid or the new root complete. Old readers/writers refuse
an unsupported selector before mutation. Mixed protected/plain and old/new
namespaces, missing keys, tampered rows, cold restart and GC/reference races need
independent tests. Full-CAS callers materialize/validate the complete logical state
and atomically replace the new root; that compatibility path may remain O(S).

## Measurement and acceptance order

1. Record isolated clone/serialization/quota costs and PB-03 stage breakdown.
2. Implement/reference-test the typed projection increment and repeat unchanged
   PB-02 load/configuration/budgets with pinned durable PostgreSQL.
3. Review a concrete representation/patch prototype and quota proof before any
   migration or runner/Storage API change.
4. Port canonical transition plans incrementally, prove reference/fast equivalence
   and refuse/fallback explicitly; keep PB-04 in progress until the required
   workloads and recovery/protection matrix meet their declared bounds.

No external services, quota widening, unresolved-work deletion, unsupported
500-agent claim or silent substitution for an older qualified artifact is part
of this proposal.
